claims.text: The literal placeholder text 'Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported' can appear in a log line, a generated file, or a resource property when an Output is treated as if it were already a plain value.

Pulumi's documentation includes an 'Output value errors' page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ that provides a rundown of symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
Resources created inside an `apply` callback will not appear in `pulumi preview` unless the output's value is already known.
Because resources created inside `apply` may not appear in `pulumi preview`, the preview output may not match the actual changes made when `pulumi up` is run.

Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page (at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/) that diagnoses errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value causes errors.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page (at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/) for resolving "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" errors.
Pulumi returns a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when another update is in progress.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors, and Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page (at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/server-errors/) for handling them.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page (at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/post-step-errors/) for troubleshooting post-step event failures and engine bugs.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page (at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/connection-issues/) for fixing network connectivity and proxy problems.

Pulumi's DIY backend troubleshooting content (at /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/#error-reading-pulumimetayaml) resolves `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors that occur when the CLI can't access a self-managed state backend.
The Pulumi CLI can raise a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error when it can't access a self-managed (DIY) state backend.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page (at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/) for handling scenarios when `pulumi destroy` fails.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page (at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/interrupted-updates/) for recovering from interrupted deployments.
Running x86_64 Pulumi binaries under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon (macOS) can cause crashes or hangs due to architecture mismatch.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page (at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/architecture-mismatch/) addressing macOS architecture mismatch crashes/hangs on Apple Silicon.
Pulumi has CI/CD troubleshooting documentation (at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/troubleshooting/) for resolving continuous integration and deployment pipeline issues.
Pulumi documents safe techniques for modifying Pulumi state files when necessary, at /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/editing-state-files/.
A recently deleted Pulumi stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi documents restoring deleted stacks at /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/restoring-deleted-stacks/.
The Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources, useful when a stuck or misbehaving resource is blocking a wider update.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics, documented at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/.
Pulumi supports installing pre-release (dev) builds to access bug fixes that haven't shipped in a stable release yet.
Pulumi documents using dev builds at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/using-dev-builds/.
Pulumi has a Community Slack (at https://slack.pulumi.com) that provides fast community support.
Pulumi has a guide for filing GitHub issues at /docs/support/filing-issues/ to report bugs in the right repository.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
Pulumi documents automatic logging at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#automatic-logging.
Pulumi offers paid support options that can be reached via a contact page at /contact/.
Pulumi offers support channels for questions or feedback via community Slack, GitHub, and a contact-support page (/support/).
Navigating to this troubleshooting page with the URL hash `#conflict` redirects the browser to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/.
The redirect for the `#conflict` hash on this page references Pulumi GitHub issue https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/issues/20846.
Navigating to this troubleshooting page with the URL hash `#verbose-logging` redirects the browser to /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging.
The redirect for the `#verbose-logging` hash on this page references Pulumi docs GitHub issue https://github.com/pulumi/docs/issues/16985.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has actually been created or updated.

If you concatenate, log, or otherwise convert a Pulumi output value to a string directly instead of going through `apply` or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default and instead silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In Pulumi's TypeScript SDK, converting an Output to a string (e.g. via template literal interpolation) silently produces a broken string containing literal text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, with no exception thrown.

In Pulumi's TypeScript SDK, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than throwing or serializing the value.

In Pulumi's Python SDK, converting an output value to a string (e.g. via an f-string) produces a broken string containing literal text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning; no exception is raised.
In Pulumi's Python SDK, passing an output to `json.dumps()` fails outright with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
Pulumi's Python SDK provides `Output.json_dumps()` as the supported way to JSON-serialize an output.

In Pulumi's Go SDK, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error rather than a runtime surprise, because Go's static typing generally prevents converting an output to a string incorrectly.

In Pulumi's C# SDK, converting an output value to a string (e.g. via string interpolation in `Console.WriteLine`) silently produces a broken string containing literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, with no exception thrown.
Pulumi's C# SDK provides `Output.Format` as an alternative to `Apply` for composing strings from outputs.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` in Pulumi's TypeScript, Python, and C# SDKs causes code that would otherwise silently produce placeholder output-to-string text to instead throw an exception at the point of the mistake.
Pulumi's TypeScript SDK provides `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` as string-composition helpers for working with outputs.
Pulumi's Python SDK provides `Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` as string-composition helpers for working with outputs.
Pulumi's Go SDK provides `pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` as string-composition helpers for working with outputs.
Pulumi's C# SDK provides `Output.Format` as a string-composition helper for working with outputs.

A value assigned to an outer variable from inside an `apply`/`Apply` callback remains unset/undefined outside that callback when read later in the program, because the callback runs asynchronously after the output resolves, which is generally after the rest of the program's top-level code has already finished running.

The delay in an output's `apply`/`Apply` callback resolving is governed by when the Pulumi engine resolves the dependency graph, not by the program's own clock, so it cannot be fixed by adding a delay.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values.
A resource's logical name is a position that cannot accept a Pulumi output value directly, unlike most resource inputs.

In a dynamically typed Pulumi SDK language, branching on an output object directly (e.g. `if (someOutput) {...}`) evaluates the output object itself rather than its eventual value, so the condition is generally always true regardless of what the output resolves to.
In a statically typed Pulumi SDK language, branching directly on an output (e.g. treating an `Output<bool>` as a `bool`) is usually a compile error.

A plain value known when a Pulumi program starts, such as a stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag, branches normally and is not subject to the output-branching problem.
In Pulumi's TypeScript, Go, and C# SDKs, passing an output as a resource's logical name, a loop bound, or a map key fails to compile because these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Pulumi's Python SDK, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string` at runtime.
In Pulumi's Python SDK, using an output as a loop bound via `range(some_output)` raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.

In Pulumi's Python SDK, using an output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; instead Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, causing the lookup to silently key on the wrong thing.

Pulumi supports restructuring dependent resources into a later, separate stack that consumes an earlier stack's outputs through a StackReference, when resource names or counts depend on data only known after an earlier resource is provisioned.

Pulumi has no supported way to block a program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an output; attempting to await or read an output's value synchronously either fails to compile, fails at runtime, or quietly returns placeholder text.
The `pulumi stack output <name>` CLI command reads a single stack output after a deployment.
A Pulumi StackReference allows one Pulumi program to consume another stack's outputs as its own inputs.
Pulumi's Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update, such as `res.Outputs` in Go, for programmatically reading deployment outputs.
